answer: The dataset was built by gathering anonymized, aggregated queries from the Google search engine that were likely to be yes/no questions. These were identified heuristically by selecting queries where the first word was in a manually constructed set of indicator words and were of sufficient length. Only questions that returned a Wikipedia page as one of the first five results were kept. These question/article pairs were then given to human annotators for further processing. The annotators labeled the pairs in a three-step process: determining if the question was good (comprehensible, unambiguous, and factual), finding a passage within the Wikipedia article that contained enough information to answer the question, and marking whether the answer was "yes" or "no". The process was expensive as it required annotators to search entire Wikipedia documents for relevant evidence and read the text carefully.
